title: Find Top Candidates Faster: October 2026 Guide
summary: Cut time to hire by reviewing resumes efficiently. Dover's ATS helps startups find top candidates fast this October 2026.
body_markdown:
Getting candidates to apply for a job opening at your startup isn’t always a problem, but[finding the right candidates](https://www.dover.com/) from a sea of resumes can quickly bottleneck your hiring pipeline. An informal survey conducted by Robin Choy suggested that about 77% of recruiters review applications without any automated sorting, so the figure is a rough estimate. Manual screening still has a place, but there’s a better way than painstakingly going through every single resume that comes through, and this guide covers tips for reviewing resumes so you can find the best candidates faster.


**TLDR:**


-


Reviewing resumes in the order received means later-applying top candidates often get missed entirely.


-


The volume of inbound applications per role has grown sharply in recent years, making manual sorting harder to keep up with at scale.


-


Sorting by fit instead of arrival order can cut the time your best candidates spend waiting to hear from you.


-


Some free ATS tools can sort, filter by persona or location, and track candidates from application to offer.


-


Some tools also pair free applicant tracking with on-demand fractional recruiters, backed by verified founder reviews, for teams that have no dedicated recruiter.


## How Startups Actually Handle the Resume Pile


Robin Choy’s survey shows how many startups still handle their resume pile: a lot of recruiters say things like, “I go through them in the order received.” Applicant tracking systems offer a better path. They don’t replace the human touch, but act as an assistant, clearing out resumes from unqualified applicants and surfacing the candidates who meet the job requirements, leaving far fewer resumes for anyone to review by hand.


## The Problem With the First-In, First-Out System When Reviewing Resumes


The first-in, first-out (FIFO) system is where resumes are reviewed in the order they arrive. It’s not necessarily the best way to find the best candidates: it can cause you to overlook highly qualified candidates who applied later and are a better fit for the job, simply because earlier applications got priority.


Few teams have time to give each application close attention, and the longer you take to work through the pile, the more likely your best candidates get hired elsewhere before you reach out. An[eye-tracking study of recruiter behavior](https://www.hrdive.com/news/eye-tracking-study-shows-recruiters-look-at-resumes-for-7-seconds/541582/) from 2018 found that recruiters spend only about 7.4 seconds on average on the initial screen of a resume, so an early applicant who gets a fast glance isn’t necessarily a better fit.


## The Importance of Time to Hire for Startups


**Time to hire** , the[days between application and offer acceptance](https://www.aihr.com/blog/time-to-hire/) , is an important metric for gauging the health of your hiring pipeline. A drawn-out process can take months to fill roles you need filled now, and[recruitment process bottlenecks](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-reduce-recruitment-process-bottlenecks-for-startups) are often the cause, delaying projects and burning out team members who pick up the slack.


A slow process can also cost you top talent. If your first contact with a strong candidate happens after they’re already three interviews deep with another company, hiring them gets much harder. Candidates who wait too long often land offers elsewhere first, which is why[reducing time to hire without sacrificing quality](https://www.hrdive.com/news/how-to-reduce-time-to-hire-without-sacrificing-quality/521032/) matters so much for startups competing for the same talent pool.

## The 2026 Application Surge: Why Manual Review Is Even Harder Now


Application volume per open role has risen sharply since 2022, according to widely cited hiring benchmarks, as candidates increasingly use AI tools to apply at scale.


AI-polished resumes are also becoming harder to tell apart at a glance, which makes filtering by fit, instead of simply by order received, matter more than ever. Some startup hiring reports suggest a majority of startup talent teams now use AI in at least one recruiting workflow.

## FAQs


### How do I reduce time to hire without missing strong candidates who apply late?


An ATS can rank applications by fit instead of arrival order, so a strong candidate who applies on day ten is not buried under everyone who applied on day one. Pairing best-match sorting with role-specific filters helps reviewers reach the strongest fits first and shortens the gap between application and first contact.


### Can I build a hiring pipeline without a dedicated recruiter?


Yes. An ATS covers sorting, filtering, scheduling, and candidate tracking without a full-time recruiter on staff. When a role needs deeper sourcing or screening, on-demand fractional recruiters can step in and work inside that same pipeline, so the team adds support without adding permanent recruiting headcount.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


An ATS organizes and ranks applicants already in the pipeline, but it does not source candidates, run outreach, screen for role-specific skills, or close offers. Teams with steady inbound volume and a few open roles can often manage with software alone. When a role is senior, specialized, or inbound volume is thin, a fractional recruiter on top of the ATS can cover the sourcing and screening the software does not. Dover pairs a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters working in the same pipeline, so the hiring team and recruiter see the same candidate status and avoid duplicate outreach.


## Final Thoughts on Reviewing Resumes for Startups


Reviewing resumes in the order received feels organized, but it tends to reward timing instead of fit, and the cost shows up as slower hiring and strong candidates accepting other offers. Success in[finding the right candidates](https://www.dover.com/) faster depends on how many roles are open and who has time to read applications, so a lightweight manual process works for some teams while sorting and filtering tools suit others. Dover’s free ATS is one example, pairing filters and Premium AI resume review with optional access to fractional recruiters inside the same pipeline.
